title: 4.5.5: Chapter Test
originalText:
1. Expand the Hindu-Arabic numeral 5,789 .

2. Evaluate the expression \(4 \times 7^3+5 \times 2^5\).

3. Rewrite \(6 \times 10^5+0 \times 10^4+8 \times 10^3+0 \times 10^2+1 \times 10^1+9 \times 10^0\) in Hindu-Arabic form.

4. Convert the Babylonian numeral to a Hindu-Arabic numeral.

Exercise \(\PageIndex{5}\)

Convert the Mayan number to a Hindu Arabic numeral.

[Figure: Mayan numeral 13 is displayed.]

[Figure: Mayan numeral 7 is displayed.]

[Figure: Mayan numeral 6 is displayed.]

6.  What base system did the Babylonians use?

Exercise \(\PageIndex{7}\)

Which system—Roman, Babylonian, Mayan—used place values?

Exercise \(\PageIndex{8}\)

Convert the Roman numeral MDXLVII to a Hindu-Arabic numeral.

Exercise \(\PageIndex{9}\)

How many symbols are needed for a base 9 system?

Exercise \(\PageIndex{10}\)

For a system in a base larger than 10, what symbols are used as digits representing more than 10?

Exercise \(\PageIndex{11}\)

Convert 132_(8) to a base 10 number.

Exercise \(\PageIndex{12}\)

List the numbers in base 4 up to 100_(4).

Exercise \(\PageIndex{13}\)

Convert 74 to a base 12 number.

Exercise \(\PageIndex{14}\)

Create the addition table for base 4.

Exercise \(\PageIndex{15}\)

Calculate \({314_6} + {453_6}\).

Exercise \(\PageIndex{16}\)

Calculate 4B1_(12) − 2A6_(12).

Exercise \(\PageIndex{17}\)

When calculating \({23_6} + {53_6}\), a student obtains 76_(6) . How do you know an error was made?

Exercise \(\PageIndex{18}\)

Create the multiplication table for base 4.

Exercise \(\PageIndex{19}\)

Calculate \({323_4} \times {132_4}\).

Exercise \(\PageIndex{20}\)

Calculate \({21_4} \div {3_4}\).
